thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> CRITICAL: inference-queue.backlog > 10000; autoscaler failing to provision. page to #eng-oncall.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-2026-4823 created and routed to current on-call.

Alex Chen: Acked. I'm looking at grafana: queue length jumped at 13:04 UTC, p95 latency 2.3s -> 5.8s, 503 rate spiking. attaching quick hits.

Alex Chen: snapshot: inference-queue.backlog = 11,350, inflight tokens up 3x. autoscaler events show repeated "FailedCreate" for node due to cloud quota.

Jamal Rao: I can confirm cluster-autoscaler logs show constant "no capacity" and repeated admission errors:
```
I0505 13:05:12 cluster-autoscaler.go:123] FailedCreate: error listing instances: quota exceeded for region us-west-2
I0505 13:05:14 cluster-autoscaler.go:125] Provisioning failed: insufficient capacity
```

Priya Shah: hmm. two immediate mitigations: 1) spin up emergency nodepool (manual) 2) throttle non-critical API keys via rate-limiter. I'll start (1) now.

Priya Shah: running:
```
# create emergency nodepool (manual override)
cloudctl compute nodepool create --name emergency-scale-1 --zone us-west-2a --size 4 --instance-type g4dn.xlarge
kubectl label nodes -l nodepool=emergency-scale-1 workload=inference
```

sre-bot: deploybot: Request accepted, provisioning nodepool emergency-scale-1. Estimated time ~3-7 minutes.

Alex Chen: good. I'm also going to scale down batch workers that are consuming shared GPU capacity to free slots (non-prod).

Casey Tran: Notifying CS: early reports from a few customers of 503s and degraded streaming responses. Initial estimate: ~2% of requests failed in last 10m; premium customers affected by higher latency. Escalating to account team.

Jamal Rao: Cloud quota is the bottleneck. I pinged cloud-support with request for emergency GPU quota increase and linked the PagerDuty ticket. message to cloud-support: "emergency quota increase for G4 in us-west-2 requested. INC-2026-4823."

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledgement recorded by Alex Chen. Escalation path: after 5m with no resolution escalate to SRE lead.

Morgan Lee: I'm live. I'll open a direct support ticket and try soft-failover for some traffic to fallback-inference (lower-capacity model) to reduce pressure. Can someone prepare routing change?

Priya Shah: Routing change: adding temporary rule in envoy to route 20% of inference traffic to fallback-inference in us-east-1. Patch:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking/v1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: inference-traffic-split
spec:
  hosts: ["api.redwood.ai"]
  http:
  - route:
    - destination: {host: inference-primary, subset: v1, weight: 80}
    - destination: {host: inference-fallback, subset: v1, weight: 20}
EOF
```

Alex Chen: applied the split. Monitoring now. backlog dipped 10% within 2m.

sre-bot: action log: manual nodepool create triggered by Priya Shah; routing split applied by Alex Chen; cloud-support ticket opened by Jamal Rao.

Jamal Rao: Nodepool is in provisioning but instances are stuck in PENDING. Cloud console shows quotas are requested, but there are also IP allocation errors for the VPC: "No available IPs in subnet" for us-west-2a.

Morgan Lee: Ok, pivot plan: we'll free up IPs by moving some non-critical subnets and then try a second provisioning in us-west-2b. Also, initiate fallback to dedicated reserved pool for top-tier customers only.

Casey Tran: Noted. Customer-impact update posted to #customer-status: "Intermittent 503s and elevated latencies for inference APIs in us-west-2. Working on mitigations. We'll follow up in 15m."

Alex Chen: manual scale command I'm running now to restart queue worker pods to force cache flush:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-queue-workers -n inference
kubectl scale deployment/inference-queue-workers --replicas=0 -n inference && sleep 10 && kubectl scale deployment/inference-queue-workers --replicas=6 -n inference
```

Priya Shah: Restart done. Workers came back up but backlog still at ~7k. Requesting a temporary increase to concurrency limit for workers to drain faster. If we increase concurrency we might raise token cost but reduces customer-visible errors.

Alex Chen: Agreed. Increasing concurrency for 15m window: set ENV WORKER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=40 -> patch applied.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: incident escalated to Morgan Lee (SRE Lead) at 13:12 UTC due to ongoing provisioning failures.

Morgan Lee: I'm on the phone with cloud-support now. They acknowledged the IP quota issue and are expediting. ETA for quota patch ~18 minutes. In meantime routing split + concurrency bump bought us some headroom.

Jamal Rao: I'm also cleaning up stale ENIs in the VPC to reclaim IPs (found ~120 unused). Running cleanup script now.

Alex Chen: backlog down to 3.2k after ENI cleanup and split, p95 latency trending down. Good. Still monitoring for regressions.

Casey Tran: CS updated: customers with priority SLAs have been given mitigations and will get a follow-up from account managers. Switching incident to "high" and will prepare post-incident summary.

Priya Shah: quick note: we should add emergency subnet expansion to runbook - this was a blind spot.

Morgan Lee: Agree. I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates. For now, Lina Kim will take over the watch after my handoff at 13:20 UTC. Lina, can you ack and pick up?

Lina Kim: Acked. I'm up next. Summary for handoff: 1) emergency nodepool created (still provisioning), 2) routing split to fallback applied, 3) concurrency bumped temporarily, 4) cloud-support ticket open, 5) backlog reduced from 11k -> 3.2k, continue to monitor until <500. Ongoing tasks: follow cloud-support ETA, verify ENI cleanup stability, coordinate final scale-down.

Alex Chen: leaving on-call notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-4823

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INCIDENT UPDATED - status: acknowledged -> mitigation-in-progress.

incident-bot: end of thread summary: manual scaling + routing split + ENI cleanup reduced backlog; cloud provider quota/IP limits are root cause; postmortem owner: Morgan Lee; handoff: Lina Kim at 13:20 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Lina Kim: I'll monitor for another 30m then start controlled ramp-down if no regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
